A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISCO and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained algorithms and experiments can be matched across the additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DISCO evaluations on DiverseHumans and MultiHuman-TestBench, component ablations, reward-weight experiments, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds supervised fine-tuning comparisons, a participant study, curriculum experiments, and generalization evaluations.

M1.justification: The original Flow-GRPO procedure, four-component facial-diversity reward, curriculum, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Appendix F.2 adds DISCO(Cloth), an adaptation replacing the ArcFace identity reward with Fashion-SigLIP clothing similarity.

E1.justification: v3 adds general compositional generation on GenEval2, out-of-training-range scenes with 8–10 people, clothing/body-type diversity evaluation, and per-person clothing and hairstyle prompts (Appendix F). The original training data, DiverseHumans, and MultiHuman-TestBench coverage remain.

E2.justification: Appendix E.1.4 adds a focused online supervised fine-tuning comparator, evaluated against DISCO in Table E.4. The original proprietary and open-source generator comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include highest-reward-sample online SFT under the same prompts and curriculum, additional curriculum bounds, a blinded study with 25 participants judging 22 image pairs, and 270 samples spanning 2–10 people. Appendix F also introduces clothing-similarity and Qwen3-VL body-type scoring and GenEval2 evaluation. The original Appendix D settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses testing RL versus additional supervised training, curriculum-bound sensitivity, agreement with human judgments, extrapolation beyond trained person counts, transfer to other visual attributes, and per-person compositional control. The earlier reward-weight, aggregation-function, computational, and artifact analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1.8 newly reports correlation analysis between automated metrics and human judgments, although the correlation coefficient type and its uncertainty are unspecified. Existing shared image-index seeds and Figure 5's 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Original main-table and retained appendix scores are unchanged. New results include SFT versus DISCO UFA of 73.0 versus 98.6 (Table E.4), curriculum-bound outcomes, clothing similarity of 0.73/0.65/0.60 for Flux/face-DISCO/clothing-DISCO (Table F.1), and GenEval2 means of 24.6 versus 27.6 for Flux and DISCO (Table F.2). Human-study correlations and larger-crowd results further expand the findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes the explicit rectified-flow interpolation and target velocity, ODE–SDE drift relationship, and trajectory-policy factorization, replacing this formal background with a shorter description and reference to Flow-GRPO. The DISCO reward mathematics and optimization objective are retained; no new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2's main claims concern facial identity diversity, counting, and maintained image quality. v3's introduction and conclusion broaden the claimed contribution to clothing/body-type diversity and preserved or improved general compositional generation, supported by the new Section 4.2.3 and Appendix F.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking RL's advantage over SFT to exploration and group-relative learning, attributing attribute transfer to broader learned distinctiveness, and attributing compositional preservation to HPSv3. It also interprets higher-count performance as generalization beyond memorization and explicitly excludes personalization from DISCO's scope. These extend the interpretations substantially, although some causal explanations lack isolating ablations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link, identifies the Fashion-SigLIP checkpoint, and documents torso cropping and Qwen3-VL body-type assessment for the new evaluations. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, baseline settings, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for CLIP, Qwen3-VL, GenEval2, concurrent diverse-video policy optimization, and Ar2Can. It briefly positions DISCO relative to concurrent video-diversity work and as a foundation for Ar2Can, while retaining the earlier related-work framework.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are revised, the mathematical preliminaries are substantially condensed, and the conclusion and limitations are rewritten. Appendix E is reorganized, a dedicated generalizability section is introduced, and ethics and reproducibility receive numbered appendix headings. These changes substantially reshape the narrative despite extensive retained technical text.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables covering SFT, curriculum bounds, attribute diversity, and GenEval2, plus four figures showing human judgments, larger-crowd performance, clothing diversity, and compositional examples. Original figure artwork is retained and relocated where needed; Figure 1 is resized and Table 2 gains a highlighted final row.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation by addressing v2's missing SFT control, human assessment of identity metrics, curriculum-bound sensitivity, and tests of extrapolation and general compositional capability. These additions support method choice and applicability while preserving the original main results. Reporting remains imperfect: the human-study correlations are incompletely specified, and the retained statement that no human subjects were used conflicts with the new 25-participant study. These limitations qualify, but do not outweigh, the broader evidential gains.
